title: Into the Easterly: EuroVelo 6 Along the Bulgarian Danube, Vidin to Cherven
subRegion: The Bulgarian Danube bank, the Danubian Plain and Rusenski Lom

bestPeriod.window: the second half of May, and the first three weeks of September
bestPeriod.avoid: July–August (35–40 °C on unshaded II-11 asphalt, and no tree cover between the river towns)

transport.note: €150–€290 (bike rental/delivery €90–€190 + BDŽ trains, bridge shuttle, transfers)

activities.note: €35–€60 (Baba Vida, Kaleto, Ivanovo, Cherven, Persina, Radetzky)

hook: Seven days on the least-ridden stretch of EuroVelo 6, where the river is a kilometre wide and the traffic is a tractor every twenty minutes. You climb a thousand metres inland to the sandstone towers of Belogradchik, drop back to a road crossing six tributary valleys, sleep in fishing towns nobody photographs, and finish at a UNESCO cave-church above a gorge. For self-sufficient riders who want distance without crowds and do not mind a headwind.

snapshot.Getting there: Sofia (SOF) is the practical gateway. BDŽ runs Sofia–Vidin daily, roughly 5–5 h 30. Finish in Ruse: BDŽ Ruse–Sofia is ~6 h 30, or fly out of Bucharest Otopeni (OTP), 75 km north across the river.

itinerary.title: Vidin, the fortress and the bridge
itinerary.morning: Arrive on the Sofia train, build or collect the bike, and ride the riverside promenade to **Baba Vida**, the only fully preserved medieval fortress in Bulgaria, its feet literally in the Danube [VERIFY: current Baba Vida entry fee and hours].
itinerary.afternoon: Spin north to the **New Europe Bridge** ramps and ride the cycle lane out over the water towards Calafat — 1,971 m of deck and the best view of Vidin there is. Return past the Ottoman **Stambol Kapiya** gate and the synagogue.
itinerary.evening: Eat on the promenade, drink Novo Selo wine, and repack. Tomorrow is the only real climbing day.

itinerary.title: The rocks above the plain
itinerary.morning: South-west out of Vidin on the Dimovo road: 25 km of gently rising farmland, then the ascent proper after **Dimovo**, where the road tips into the western Balkan foothills and stays up for 20 km.
itinerary.afternoon: Roll into **Belogradchik** at about 520 m, close to a thousand metres above the river. Take the last steep pitch to **Kaleto**, the fortress built into the sandstone towers themselves — Roman foundations, Ottoman walls, rock doing the work of ramparts [VERIFY: current Kaleto and Belogradchik Rocks entry fee].
itinerary.evening: Walk to the **Zbegovete** viewpoint for sunset, when the rock turns properly red. It is cold after dark up here even in a summer week.

itinerary.title: Back down to the river
itinerary.morning: A 12 km spur to the **Magura Cave** at Rabisha — bat colony, and prehistoric wall paintings drawn in bat guano — before the long descent [VERIFY: current Magura Cave hours].
itinerary.afternoon: Drop north-east through Dimovo to **Archar** — Roman **Ratiaria**, capital of Dacia Ripensis, now a ploughed field with a fence and a sign. Join **II-11** and turn east.
itinerary.evening: Into **Lom**, Bulgaria's second Danube port, for river fish on the quay. The wind will have been in your face for 40 km; this is the day you learn the week's rhythm.

itinerary.title: Two valleys and a nuclear town
itinerary.morning: East out of Lom across the **Tsibritsa** and the **Ogosta** — the first two rungs of the washboard, each a 70 m drop and climb with nothing to break the wind on the rim.
itinerary.afternoon: **Kozloduy**: the nuclear plant's stacks own the skyline, but stop for the **Radetzky**, a full-size replica of the Austrian paddle steamer Hristo Botev's rebels seized in 1876, moored where they landed [VERIFY: current Radetzky museum-ship hours].
itinerary.evening: On to **Oryahovo**, a hill town rising steeply off its own ferry terminal (the crossing runs to Bechet, Romania). Guesthouses sit on the upper terrace; the dusk view down the river pays for the last climb.

itinerary.title: Along the Iskar mouth to Nikopol
itinerary.morning: The best surface of the week: a resurfaced run east from Oryahovo across open grain country, the river appearing and disappearing on the left.
itinerary.afternoon: At **Gigen**, detour 2 km to **Ulpia Oescus**, the Roman colony at the mouth of the Iskar — a large, quiet, half-excavated field of foundations and column drums with almost no visitors.
itinerary.evening: Into **Nikopol**, the steepest town on the route, its ruined Byzantine and Ottoman fortress on the bluff above the Turnu Măgurele ferry. Fish soup, then bed — tomorrow is short and the hours belong on the island.

itinerary.title: The island and the marshes
itinerary.morning: An easy 12 km to **Belene**. Report to the **Persina Nature Park** visitor centre in town before riding the dykes — the park covers the whole Bulgarian Danube island complex and **Persin** is the largest island in the Bulgarian Danube [VERIFY: current Persina visitor centre opening hours and whether an island permit is required].
itinerary.afternoon: Persin's restored marshes are reintroduction ground for Dalmatian pelican, pygmy cormorant and ferruginous duck — ride the compacted dyke slowly, with binoculars. The island also held Bulgaria's principal labour camp; there is a memorial.
itinerary.evening: On to **Svishtov**, the northernmost point of Bulgaria: Kolyu Ficheto's **Sveta Troitsa** church, and the Roman legionary fortress of **Novae** on the eastern edge of town.

itinerary.title: The gorge, the cave church and little Vienna
itinerary.morning: Skip the truck-heavy 35 km of II-52: take the early bus or BDŽ connection with the bike to **Byala**, then ride south-east through Polsko Kosovo to **Dve Mogili** [VERIFY: current Svishtov–Byala bus and bike-carriage arrangement].
itinerary.afternoon: Drop into **Rusenski Lom Nature Park** and the Cherni Lom gorge to **Cherven**, a 12th–14th-century fortress town on a meander spur, reached by footbridge and a stiff walk. Then the gorge road north to the **Ivanovo Rock-Hewn Churches**, UNESCO-listed since 1979 — the Church of the Holy Virgin is a cave gallery in the cliff with 14th-century frescoes, up a steel stair [VERIFY: current Ivanovo entry fee and closing day].
itinerary.evening: Twenty easy kilometres north into **Ruse**. Finish on **ploshtad Svoboda** beneath the **Dohodno Zdanie**, among the neo-baroque façades that earned the "little Vienna" tag, and eat somewhere with a tablecloth.

accommodationStrategy.name: Upper-town guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: the rocks are floodlit and the town empties when the day coaches leave, so an overnight buys the site alone at dusk and again at 08:00. Courtyards take bikes; most houses cook dinner if you ask at booking.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–3 weeks ahead for May and September weekends, by phone or Booking.com; midweek walk-ins are fine [VERIFY: current Belogradchik guesthouse rates].

accommodationStrategy.name: Riverfront guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: both sit on the bank above the ferry terminal — secure yard, a 06:30 start straight onto II-11, dinner within 200 m, and the week's lowest rates at €20–€30.
accommodationStrategy.booking: a week ahead or on the day by phone. Outside August nobody is competing for beds.

accommodationStrategy.name: Central hotels around ploshtad Svoboda
accommodationStrategy.description: end-of-trip logistics — inside the neo-baroque core, 10 minutes from the BDŽ station for the bike train to Sofia, close to the bridge plaza for a Bucharest flight, with lockable luggage rooms.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead. Ruse fills with business travellers, so Tuesday and Wednesday are tightest.

logistics.connectivity: A1, Yettel and Vivacom cover the river road and every town on it; coverage drops in the Cherni Lom gorge and on parts of the Persin dykes. Download the route offline — EuroVelo 6 signage here is sporadic and cannot be navigated by.
logistics.emergency: **112**, with English-speaking operators. Quote the II-11 kilometre marker if you can see one; it is the fastest way to be located between towns.
logistics.weather: Continental and extreme. May can hold a 12 °C day of rain and a 32 °C day in the same week; July hits 38 °C with no shade between tributary valleys. Storms build on the plain late afternoon and cross fast. Carry 2.5 litres — gaps between village taps run to 25 km.
logistics.bookingWindows: Nothing needs months of notice except the Sofia bike delivery (4–6 weeks) and a Ruse hotel midweek (3–4 weeks).
logistics.money: Bulgaria uses the **euro**, lev fixed at 1 EUR = 1.95583 BGN, dual pricing still displayed. Cards work in Vidin, Lom, Svishtov and Ruse. **Carry €80–€120 in small notes** — village shops, the Cherven ticket hut, ferry kiosks and guesthouses between Lom and Nikopol are cash-first.
logistics.transportRules: The **Ruse–Giurgiu bridge cannot be ridden**; the **Vidin–Calafat bridge can**. Oryahovo–Bechet and Nikopol–Turnu Măgurele ferries take bikes.
logistics.permits: No permit for the EuroVelo 6 line. **Persina** restricts parts of the island complex in the breeding season and asks visitors to register at Belene; **Rusenski Lom** is marked paths only. No wild camping in either. Lights and reflective gear outside built-up areas are legally required — II-11 is unlit and busy with farm traffic at dusk.

proTips: **Ride the long eastbound days before 11:00.** The easterly is a morning breeze and an afternoon wall. On Days 4 and 5, leaving at 06:30 and finishing by 14:00 is the whole difference.
**Sleep in Belogradchik, don't day-trip it.** Sofia operators arrive at midday and leave by five; an overnight gives you the towers at dusk and dawn with nobody in them.

**Book the bike delivery before the flights.** Sofia fleets are finite in May and September, and a Vidin drop plus a Ruse collection is a 600 km round trip for the operator — it is the one piece that can fail.
**Learn three words:** *"чешма"* (public drinking fountain — ask in every village), *"баничарница"* (the pastry shop that opens at 06:00) and *"колело"* (bicycle).
**Keep the Oryahovo ferry as a fallback.** If wind or a mechanical wrecks Day 5, the Romanian bank is flatter, faster and better connected back to Bucharest.
**Eat river fish.** Danube carp (*шаран*) and catfish in Lom, Nikopol and Svishtov cost a third of the Black Sea equivalent. Order it grilled, not fried.

raw.Daily legs: D1 Vidin loop 24 km / +140 m. D2 Vidin → Belogradchik 55 km / +980 m. D3 Belogradchik → Archar → Lom 80 km / +320 / −850 m. D4 Lom → Kozloduy → Oryahovo 92 km / +560 m. D5 Oryahovo → Gigen → Nikopol 76 km / +520 m. D6 Nikopol → Belene → Svishtov 58 km / +330 m. D7 Byala → Cherven → Ivanovo → Ruse 77 km / +690 m.
raw.Surface split: Roughly **82% asphalt, 11% gravel or compacted dyke track, 7% badly patched or broken asphalt**. The spine is **republican road II-11**, which shadows the river from Vidin to Svishtov: two lanes, no shoulder, low traffic, and surface quality that changes at every municipal boundary. Gravel is concentrated on the **Persina** dykes and the **Rusenski Lom** tracks. Ride **35–40 mm tyres minimum**; a gravel bike or rigid tourer is right, a 25 mm road bike is not.
raw.The terrain is not flat: The river is flat; the road is not. The **Danubian Plain is a washboard** — the Lom, Tsibritsa, Ogosta, Iskar, Vit, Osam and Yantra each cut a 60–120 m valley across your line of travel, and II-11 drops into and climbs out of every one. Expect **500–700 m of ascent on a "flat" river day**, and nearly **1,000 m on the Belogradchik climb**, from about 35 m at the Danube to 520 m in town and 600 m at the Kaleto gate.
raw.The wind: A **persistent easterly to north-easterly** runs the corridor, strongest in spring and often 20–30 km/h through the afternoon. Riding west to east you ride **into it** most of the week — deliberate, since it front-loads the wind onto the short sheltered western days. Want it behind you? Run the route in reverse from Ruse.
raw.Bike rental and delivery: No walk-in rental counter exists in Vidin. Bikes come from Sofia: **Odysseia-In**, **Penguin Travel** and **Cycling Bulgaria** rent touring and gravel bikes and will deliver to Vidin and collect in Ruse, typically €90–€190 for the week including transfer [VERIFY: current rental and delivery rates]. Ruse has bike shops around ulitsa Aleksandrovska [VERIFY: current Ruse bike-shop names and hours]. Carry two tubes, a folding tyre and a chain link — between Lom and Nikopol there is nothing.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation: Danube-town guesthouses have a courtyard, shed or garage; ask for *"стая за колело"* and the bike comes inside. Nowhere here has a formal bike room, and nowhere needs one.
raw.Trains with bikes (BDŽ): Bikes travel in the **baggage compartment of trains marked with a bicycle symbol**; buy a separate bike ticket at the counter, around €2 (4 BGN) [VERIFY: current BDŽ bicycle-ticket price]. Sofia–Vidin and Ruse–Gorna Oryahovitsa–Sofia services generally take them; some expresses do not, and on a crowded train the guard decides. Buy it at the station — conductors will not.
raw.Bridges to Romania: The **New Europe Bridge, Vidin–Calafat** (2013) has a **separate pedestrian and cycle lane** and can be ridden [VERIFY: current cyclist access and whether a fee applies]. The **Danube Bridge, Ruse–Giurgiu** (1954) is **closed to cyclists and pedestrians**; reach Giurgiu by bridge shuttle minibus or a lift arranged at the customs plaza, roughly €10–€15 [VERIFY: current Ruse bridge shuttle operation and fare].
